answer: One defence is rate-limited reputation decay. Picture the agent economy as a wharf: every identity docked there must keep landing small, peer-verified deliveries, and trust leaks away between them. The delta of reputation an agent can gain per epoch is capped, so a fresh identity cannot be pumped up quickly, while idle ones spiral toward zero. An attacker running a thousand puppets must feed each one real, graded work for many epochs just to keep it afloat, so cost scales linearly with the number of fakes while the payoff of any single identity stays bounded.
